claims.claim: Chambers & Kalff (1985; abstract) put the angiosperm limit at ~21 % of surface light and the charophyte limit at ~11 %
claims.note: No full text. The abstract says growing-season irradiance at the maximum depth of colonization was about 1800 J/cm² for angiosperms AND bryophytes and 1200 J/cm² for charophytes, 'on average, 21 and 11%' of the PAR incident on the water surface. So the paper's '(abstract)' tag is accurate; the 21 % also applies to bryophytes, and it is a mean across lakes (eight southern Québec lakes plus literature lakes), not a threshold.

claims.claim: the depth of 21 % (and 11 %) of surface light with Kd = 2.70/SD: 2.02 / 2.25 / 2.60 m (2.86 / 3.19 / 3.68 m)
claims.note: The percentages are this entry's (abstract only); Kd = 2.70/SD is Koenings & Edmundson's. Redone z = ln(1/f)/Kd: 2.02, 2.25, 2.60 and 2.86, 3.19, 3.68 — right. The abstract's shares are of PAR incident on the water surface, while Kd attenuates light below the surface, so these depths ignore the loss at the surface itself (they are slightly too deep) — a small bias to state if the full text confirms 'incident'.
